description: Branch R-SORT-3 Traversal consequences (row-locator tie break) on a ACCDB. Equal keys are inserted with IDs in a scrambled order, (ID,K): (5,a) (8,b) (3,a) (2,b) (9,a) (4,c) (1,a) (6,b) (7,a). TA has non-unique IX_K built before the rows, TB builds it after the rows, TD has no index. Reads the IX_K forward and backward walks of TA and TB, and SQL ORDER BY K, ORDER BY K, ID and ORDER BY K DESC on all three. Then IDs 3 and 7 are deleted and IDs 3 (K = a) and 11 (K = a) inserted, and everything is read again. Asks whether ties order by ID, by insertion order, or by row position, and how the SQL order and a delete and reinsert differ.
retentionNote: Designed r-q-fmt-sort probe (A-02); complete capture of the ACE answer.
